blocks.text: «In oblique cases the numbers always agree in case with the noun to which they refer (**двум студентам**; **с тремя книгами**; **на четырёх грузовиках**). Note also the “**Ь**” and the stress in the Instrumental case of “**ЧЕТЫРЕ**” — “**ЧЕТЫРЬМЯ**”.» The accusative: «**два, две or двух**» — the genitive form with an animate noun.
DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 70–71, pp. 26 and 35. · Every form on this page is the OpenCorpora dictionary's own (CC BY-SA 4.0), put together by the rules quoted above.

Real sentences: from the library's public-domain books (author and title above each), and from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), shown with their translation. The numeral is blanked; type it in the form the sentence needs. ё and е are both accepted.

exercises.q: Ты можешь назвать две страны, которые омываются ___ (3) океанами?
exercises.prompt: *Can you name the two countries in the world that border on three oceans?*
exercises.why: **три → тремя** (instr.: agrees with океанами (instrumental plural)). Numerals decline like adjectives in the plural; every part of a compound numeral declines.

exercises.why: **два → двум** (dat.: по + dative). Numerals decline like adjectives in the plural; every part of a compound numeral declines.

exercises.q: Роман — роман в ___ (4) частях!
exercises.why: **четыре → четырех** (prep.: agrees with частях (prepositional plural)). Numerals decline like adjectives in the plural; every part of a compound numeral declines.

exercises.q: И началось и продолжалось в течение ___ (4) лет.
exercises.why: **четыре → четырех** (gen.: agrees with лет (genitive plural)). Numerals decline like adjectives in the plural; every part of a compound numeral declines.

whys.two: «In oblique cases the numbers always agree in case with the noun to which they refer (двум студентам; с тремя книгами; на четырёх грузовиках). Note also the “Ь” and the stress in the Instrumental case of “ЧЕТЫРЕ” — “ЧЕТЫРЬМЯ”.» The accusative: «два, две or двух» — the genitive form with an animate noun. — DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 70–71, pp. 26 and 35.
